scope: Theorem 2.1 (Ordinary handle units) of the manuscript “Purely cosmetic surgery on knots in the three-sphere” (preprints/Purely-Cosmetic-Surgery-on-Knots-in-the-Three-Sphere-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 306 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ee916c92b825a868), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let C(Yj; Z) be the irreducible, unframed instanton complex with the determinants just specified. Compatible small perturbations and coherent orientations can be chosen so that the rigid counts define integral chain maps, and the rigid and interval counts have the following properties over F2. (i) Each rigid meridional handle map Yr −→ Yr+1, for r = 0, 1, is a unit whenever its de- terminant has the specified end restrictions. The rigid count on their composite is their composition up to chain homotopy. Denote this composite by f+ : C(Y0) −→ C(Y2). (ii) On the path 2 −→ ∞ −→ 0, let Fl, A be the capped Seifert classes of squares −2, 0, respectively, with Fl · A = 0, and let Sl = A − Fl. Choose the base determinant c(Fl, A) = (0, 1) and the two determinants c + e PD(Sl), e = 0, 1, identified off Sl. The sum modulo two of the interval counts of actual index −1 is a unit g+ : C(Y2; F2) −→ C(Y0; F2). (iii) The mirror construction, read backwards, gives units f− : C(Y−2) −→ C(Y0) on the rigid path through −1, and g− : C(Y0; F2) −→ C(Y−2; F2) on 0 −→ ∞ −→ −2. For g− the base evaluations are (1, 0) and the second determinant differs by the Poincaré dual of the intervening (−2)-sphere. For the summed interval maps, each summand has an integral orientation; the assertion that the sum is a chain map and a unit is required only after reduction modulo two. End identifications, including any tensor automorphisms, are fixed before composing the maps.
